source_issues.detail: src_1 (AoPS wiki, IMO 2022 P6) and src_2 (Evan Chen notes) are cited with empty excerpts and declared 'context only'. Not retrieved (no browsing) and not treated as checked; they are not load-bearing: every lemma used is re-proved in §0–§1. No result is taken on citation and no misattribution is made.

src_3 (problema-2/submission/parte-1.md) is an internal repo file not included in the envelope. The candidate restates its Lemmas with proofs, so the argument does not depend on reading it. Attach the file if a citation trail is wanted.

computation_issues.detail: Python version not recorded (standard library only; orchestrator re-runs with python3 succeeded). Reported timings (0.24s/0.39s) differ slightly from trusted re-runs (0.47s/0.71s) — immaterial, both far below 10 minutes. code_2, code_4, code_6, code_7 import code_1 as module `conta_cammini`; the artifact bundle must keep that filename.

code_6 (200k random labellings, exact integers) and code_7 (annealing, 8 seeds all reaching 88, exact scoring) are correctly labelled evidence-only and are not used in the proof. The annealing optimum (5 valleys, 88 paths) is consistent with Lemma 7 (X=3, |H|=1, i=2, q=13: 4q=47+5).

rule_violations.detail: The supplied rules are the team's internal defaults (CLAUDE.md), which themselves instruct the Referee to flag as MISSING every point depending on the real regulation. Points to close with the official rules: (a) admissibility of a computer-assisted lower bound with a written reduction (under supplied rules it is permitted: allow_computation=true, reduction to (★) proved in §2, covered set declared, exact integer arithmetic, <1s runtime); (b) required reporting format for node counts / wall-clock; (c) whether the labelling format (32 comma-separated 0/1 strings, coordinate 1 on the left) matches the checker's convention — irrelevant for the value, which is what is scored. This is the only reason the verdict is not PASS: evidence and reproducibility checks are complete.

claim_provenance.notes: Lower bound: hand case analysis (§1–§2) reduces T<=87 to predicate (★): an independent 12-set I and u∉I with Q_5−(I∪{u}) a forest. I checked the algebra of Lemmas 5–7 and the case split to the extent needed to confirm the scripts test exactly (★): code_2 enumerates all independent 12-sets containing vertex 0 (XOR translations are transitive automorphisms preserving (★)) and every u outside, forest test by edges = vertices − components; code_3 enumerates all 3672 independent 12-sets without symmetry via the bipartite split and union-find. Outputs (1377/27540/0 and 3672/73440/0, consistent via 3672·12/32=1377) were reproduced by the orchestrator. Upper bound: explicit labelling, bijection asserted, 88 reproduced by recursion (code_4) and by explicit DFS (code_5), identical valleys and order as in §4. Full mathematical review of the case analysis is Referee A's remit; permitted_by_rules is under the supplied internal rules, pending the official regulation.

report.reproducibility_notes: All seven artifacts were re-run by the orchestrator from a clean copy: code_2 (0.5s) and code_3 (0.7s) reproduce the exact counts claimed with 0 acyclic complements; code_4 and code_5 both print 88 with the same 8 valleys and the same 32-vertex order as §4; code_6 confirms the identity on 200k random labellings; code_7 reaches 88 on all 8 seeds (79s). Standard-library Python, integer arithmetic throughout; proof-relevant scripts (code_2..code_5) run in under 2 seconds total, far below the 10-minute limit. The two lower-bound certificates use genuinely different enumerations (backtracking with symmetry vs. bipartite bitmask scan) and different acyclicity tests, so they are independently checkable. Evidence checks are complete; the verdict is PARTIAL solely because the official competition rules are not supplied.
